title: Selector/labels maps with any templated value must void entirely
context: extractLiteralLabelMap's guard rejecting partially-templated maps was untested and survived mutation testing. Without it, a Service selector with `app: {{ .Values.name }}` and `tier: web` would incorrectly resolve to just the literal `tier: web`, creating false-positive Service-to-workload reference edges.
decision: Reinforced the guard that rejects an entire labels/selector map if ANY value is templated (not just block-form templates). Added three new tests that explicitly catch the mutation: two unit tests for selector and pod-template-labels cases, and one end-to-end indexer test confirming no false-positive edges.
consequences: Selectors/labels with any templated value now deterministically void to null, eliminating false-positive edges
Conservative rejection of uncertainty rather than permissive partial matching
Prevents Helm-templated deployment selectors from generating spurious cross-resource references
Regression protection: mutation of the guard is now immediately caught by test suite
alternatives_rejected: Partially accept literal keys and skip templated ones (creates strictly more-permissive false-positive matches)
Only check for block-form templates (same-line templated values would still bypass the check)

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Partially accept literal keys and skip templated ones (creates strictly more-permissive false-positive matches)
